$comment: ★★ A FOREIGN MEMBER READS A LIBRARY DATUM THROUGH THE GOT (P68 round 11, lane `xa`: the import half of D-LK-ELF-READER-REFUSES-GOTPCREL-BLOCKS-REAL-GLIBC-MEMBERS and D-LK-ELF-AARCH64-EXEC-REFUSES-GOT-RELOCATIONS). The prebuilt archives hold one member each (source and flags in main.c) whose code reaches libc's `stdout` through its GOT slot. The link mints ONE slot for `stdout` and rewrites every reference into a direct one to it; `stdout` being a library DATUM, the slot is filled by the loader through a row against the symbol, so the member loads the datum's address from it. ✔MEASURED 2026-09-24: gcc -no-pie and -pie run this main.c with each archive to 42, and so does this link; on main's build before this change the x86_64 archive was refused at READ (relocation type 42) and the aarch64 one at the link's kind unifier. Exit codes: 2 — the member's `&stdout` is not the program's; 1 — its value is not; 42 — both are. The `release` arm links the same archives under the shipped release pipeline. The same source in gcc's DEFAULT x86_64 code names `stdout` directly and is refused: examples/c/foreign_member_reads_a_library_datum_directly_refused.

prebuiltLibraries.$comment: gcc 13.3.0 `-O2 -fPIC -c` of the member quoted in main.c + GNU ar `rcsD`: two R_X86_64_REX_GOTPCRELX against `stdout`. The witness is the member's own definition.

aarch64-linux-gnu-gcc 13.3.0 `-O2 -c` (default codegen) of the same member + aarch64-linux-gnu-ar `rcsD`: two R_AARCH64_ADR_GOT_PAGE + R_AARCH64_LD64_GOT_LO12_NC pairs against `stdout`. The witness is the member's own definition.
